input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right on one month's notice effective at the end of a calendar month, which meets the preferred notice standard, and IBM has no convenience right during a term (only 90 days' non-renewal notice under 3.2) — both consistent with the playbook. The material failure is the exit price: 3.4(b) conditions the right on payment of open-ended early termination charges set in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments, with no cap, and Section 3.5 provides no refund of prepaid Charges. An uncapped termination charge can exceed the fallback ceiling of three months' fees and effectively negate the convenience right. Our redline caps the charge at three months' recurring Charges and adds a pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges; we adopted the fallback fee cap rather than deleting the charge entirely given the short notice period already conceded.

ops.oldText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
ops.newText: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services, and IBM will refund to Customer any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We capped the early termination charges at three months' recurring Charges and added a refund of prepaid Charges, since our playbook position is a convenience exit without penalty and Attachment A charges are currently open-ended.
proposal.summary: Cap convenience-termination charges at three months' fees and require refund of prepaid Charges.
